subject: PrivNet rolling upgrade - intermittent control handshake variance and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Huang <rachel.huang@fidelishealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Fidelis Health Platform Team <support@fidelishealth.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@fidelishealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected control handshakes during rolling upgrade - impact on inference

Hi Mateo / Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike in 502/504 errors and elevated p99 latency ~07:45 PDT as your scheduled rolling upgrade hit our private cluster. The errors show up as "control handshake timeout" in our sidecar logs; a subset of inferences failed to connect to the control plane and were retried by our client with exponential backoff. Impact: ~7% of requests for a 10-minute window failed entirely (user-facing errors).

I attached a small slice of logs that show the handshake traces and the upgrade-timeline.csv exported from our telemetry. We're on a Private (VPC) deployment in us-west-2. Can you confirm whether there was a control-plane certificate or leader election change around that time?

We need:
- Immediate status and mitigation plan
- Whether any data was dropped or requeued
- ETA for permanent fix or rollback

Thanks — this is visible in prod and a priority for our incident review.

—Rachel
Rachel Huang
Sr. Platform SRE, Fidelis Health
Attachments: privnet-diagnostics-logs-0618.txt, upgrade-timeline-0618.csv

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Huang <rachel.huang@fidelishealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Fidelis Health Platform Team <support@fidelishealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected control handshakes during rolling upgrade - impact on inference

Rachel — thank you for the quick heads-up and the logs; we see the same failure signature in our telemetry. Immediate notes:

- We observed a short window of elevated control-plane latency starting at 07:43 PDT concurrent with a canary batch of the rolling upgrade. Some agents experienced handshake retries when connecting to the new control plane leader.
- No evidence of data loss: requests that failed on handshake were either retried by your client or fell back to cached responses. We will continue to verify integrity against request IDs you attached.

Immediate mitigation (already executed):
1) We paused the next canary batch at 07:50 PDT and removed the in-flight upgrade job for the remaining hosts in your pool.
2) We applied a temporary increase to control-plane connection timeout from 2s to 5s for your tenant to reduce early failures while we investigate.

Next steps / bridge:
- We're standing up a 30-minute bridge at 09:00 PDT to walk through telemetry and telemetry-aligned logs (link: https://app.redwood.io/meet/privnet-bridge-20280618). Can you join?
- Our oncall engineer Aditya (cc'd) will post a short root-cause hypothesis and initial runbook within 60 minutes.

I'll follow up after the first postmortem pass. Apologies for the impact — we take this seriously.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: bridge agenda (agenda.txt)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage — control handshake variance during rolling upgrade

Internal notes (do not forward to customer without editing):

Summary of telemetry:
- Canary upgrade at ~07:39–07:47 PDT. Control-plane RPC latency spiked to 600–900ms for 90s, then back to baseline. Agent-side handshake retried at ~2s timeouts and raised 502s.
- Leader election occurred at 07:43:12 PDT on the management pod set (race with certificate refresh hook).

Preliminary root cause hypothesis:
- A certificate hot-reload hook for the control-plane caused a brief lock (mutex) during the leader handoff which amplified RPC latency under the canary batch load. This caused some agent handshakes to hit the short 2s client timeout.

Proposed action plan (short):
A) Reproduce in staging with same sequence: orchestrate cert-rotation + leader swap under canary load.
B) Patch: remove blocking work from hot-reload path and change leader election grace window to 4s.
C) Rollout: 1) small staged canary (1 host) 2) 10% 3) 50% with monitoring and automatic rollback on >1% errors.

Customer-facing steps to propose: rollback the remaining upgrade for Fidelis (done), temporary timeout increase (done), schedule a controlled re-rollout with the patched build once validated (ETA 24–48h).

Action items:
- Evelyn: prepare reproduction job in staging (ETA 2h)
- Kimberly: draft customer-friendly runbook text and a timeline for a safe re-rollout (ETA 3h)
- Mateo: coordinate customer bridge and approvals

Aditya
Senior Software Engineer — Inference Runtime

Date: 2028-06-19T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Rolling upgrade follow-up and runbook — control handshake variance (post-incident summary)

Rachel / Fidelis team — thank you for joining the bridge and for the logs. Below is a concise post-incident summary and the steps we will take to prevent recurrence. Please let us know if you'd like this captured in an RFC-style postmortem for your records.

Event timeline (concise):
- 07:39 PDT — Canary batch rollout started in your private pool.
- 07:43:12 PDT — Control-plane leader election coincided with a cert hot-reload hook.
- 07:43:12–07:44:45 PDT — Observed elevated control-plane RPC latency (peak ~900ms).
- 07:50 PDT — We paused the remaining upgrade jobs for your pool and increased tenant handshake timeout from 2s -> 5s to reduce failed requests.

Impact: ~7% of requests returned transient 502/504 over the 90s window. No indication of permanent data loss; most requests were retried by clients or served from cache.

Root cause (short):
- A blocking hot-reload task invoked during certificate refresh introduced mutex contention in the control-plane codepath, which, combined with a leader election event during a canary load, caused temporary RPC latency amplification.

Corrective actions (we will implement):
1) Code change to make cert hot-reload non-blocking and remove synchronous work from the critical RPC path (deploy candidate: 2028-06-20).
2) Leader election grace window increase from 1s -> 4s to reduce overlap risk with hot-reload events.
3) Improved canary gating: hold canary batch until cert-rotation sweep completes for the zone.
4) Tenant-level safety knobs: automatic handshake-timeout adaptors during upgrades.

Planned rollout: staging repro + validation (June 18–19), canary deploy to a small internal test pool (June 20 morning), then controlled re-rollout for customers with accepted maintenance windows (June 21–22). We will share the precise maintenance window and a pre-upgrade checklist for Fidelis.

Compensation and next steps:
- We will credit one day of Dedicated capacity usage for the impacted window (applies to DF-4821) and are open to a deeper credit discussion if fidelity testing shows greater customer impact.
- Action item: Kimberly will send a plain-language runbook and the proposed maintenance window options by EOD today.

Attachments included for your review: privnet-diagnostics-logs-0618.txt (selected traces), upgrade-timeline-0618.csv, bridge-call-recording-0618.mp3.

If you'd like a formal postmortem doc with charts and raw traces included, we can produce that within 72 hours.

Apologies again for the interruption — we appreciate your patience and partnership.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
